task.description:
Implement REQ-062 (sub-process invocation runtime half) exactly per the PASSED design lib/letflow/design/req062-sub-process-runtime.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ062-20260819, already checked out -- verify with git branch --show-current before touching anything). Follow WF-02 Step 2a's procedure in full (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md): implement lib/**/*.ex per the design, write priv/repo/migrations/*.exs per the design's DB spec, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix ecto.migrate (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2, Docker fallback per docs/anti-patterns.md if no toolchain), mix format --check-formatted, then the self-review checklist (no tenant/user string interpolation into raw SQL, no unresolved {:ok,_}= on external-I/O paths, one supervised process per instance preserved if touching process_instance.ex/instance_supervisor.ex, new public functions have @doc, all callers of any changed signature still compile). Pay particular attention to design OQ-1 (the assumed SUB_PROCESS definition-reference attribute name/resolution path) -- if it turns out wrong against the actual definitions schema, fix it and note the correction, don't silently guess something else. Use a migration version-number prefix that does not collide with any existing priv/repo/migrations/ file (docs/anti-patterns.md documents a real prior collision class here -- check existing prefixes first).

REWORK ITERATION 1 (ORCH review, not a new agent's finding): your own result.issues on the completed pass correctly flagged, but did not fix, that lib/letflow/engine/reconstruction.ex (REQ-053, status: done) has no apply_event/3 clause for the new SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED event type this branch introduces -- its catch-all now surfaces {:unrecognized_event_type, "SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED", _} for it. REQ-053's own AC1 requires replay through transition/3 to reproduce the persisted projection field-for-field for EVERY event type an instance's log can contain; SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED becomes exactly such a type as of this branch, so this is a regression this run itself introduces, not an unrelated pre-existing gap -- per core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything rule, fix it within this run rather than filing it forward. Add an apply_event/3 clause for %{event_type: "SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED"} mirroring the existing TASK_COMPLETED clause's shape (read the event's persisted fields -- likely the same output_variables/node_id-equivalent shape append_completion_multi/5 already writes when it persists this event type in the live path, check what fields it actually writes to the events table and read those same fields back here), merging output variables per the same VariableMerge.merge/3 + build_parent_merge_variables/2 filtering logic used by the live completion path (do not duplicate the filtering logic inline -- call the same Letflow.Engine.SubProcess function the live path calls), then dispatching the equivalent of dispatch_sub_process_completion/4 so state converges to the same post-completion shape the live path produces. Do NOT touch the other two flagged-but-not-blocking issues (OQ-3 nested sub-process activation, the split/join-not-supported guard) -- those remain correctly out of this requirement's scope, leave them as-is.

REWORK ITERATION 2: TEST-RUNNER (Step 4) ran the full suite and found 86 failures, all traced to REQ-062's own changes, two distinct causes that are your fix, plus a third that is TEST-DESIGNER's (handled separately -- do not touch test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs's {:sub_process_completed} test yourself). Fix ONLY these two: (a) priv/repo/migrations/20260819045553_add_sub_process_parent_columns.exs was never added to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest -- despite the migration file's own header comment stating registration is mandatory -- so provisioned tenant schemas are missing parent_instance_id/parent_token_id, and any query touching instance_projections's full row (EventStore.active_instance_guard/3, hit by create/2, complete_task/3, cancel_instance/3, EventStore.append/2) raises Postgrex.Error 42703 column does not exist. Register the migration in the manifest, matching the exact convention every other tenant-scoped migration there already follows. (b) lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex's @node_type_map has no "SUB_PROCESS" => :SUB_PROCESS entry, so every SUB_PROCESS node fixture parses as :unknown_node_type and Engine.create/2 fails with node_type_not_yet_implemented before any of your sub-process dispatch code ever runs -- add the missing map entry, matching the existing entries' exact shape (check what :HUMAN_TASK/:SERVICE_TASK/:TIMER look like in the same map). After both fixes: mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix ecto.migrate, and re-run a scoped subset (MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/engine_test.exs) to confirm both classes of failure are actually gone -- do not run the full suite yourself, that's TEST-RUNNER's job again after TEST-DESIGNER's fix also lands.

REWORK ITERATION 3 (final rework attempt -- max_rework is 3): your own iteration-2 pass fixed the two originally-assigned failure classes but surfaced two further, different bugs while confirming the scoped subset, leaving 6 of 42 tests in test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs failing. These are two DISTINCT new bugs, not the same failure recurring, so no strategy change is required, just fix both: (a) CaseClauseError in Letflow.Engine.append_sub_process_completion_cascade_multi/6 (lib/letflow/engine.ex around line 1678) against a %TokenRecord{} shape it doesn't handle -- read the actual case statement, find what shape it expects vs. what a real TokenRecord struct actually looks like at that call site (likely a mismatch between the pure Token struct used inside Transition/SubProcess's pre-Multi logic and the persisted TokenRecord schema struct used once tokens are loaded from the DB -- check which one is actually being passed in at that call site and reconcile), affecting 4 tests (AC3/AC8 output-side, AC4, AC5). (b) Protocol.UndefinedError -- no Jason.Encoder derived for Letflow.EventStore.Registry.ValidationFailure, hit when an input-schema-violation error gets serialized into an event/error payload -- add a `@derive Jason.Encoder` (or the equivalent existing convention this codebase already uses for other structs that get JSON-encoded into event payloads -- check how a comparable existing struct, e.g. ExecutionError's own error struct, handles this) to ValidationFailure, affecting the AC3/AC8 input-schema-violation test. After both fixes: mix compile --warnings-as-errors, then MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/engine_test.exs again -- all 42+ tests in that scoped run must pass before you mark this PASS. If you cannot get to fully green within this iteration, mark PARTIAL (not PASS) and name exactly what remains broken -- do not report PASS without having actually run and observed a green scoped run.
acceptance_criteria: a token entering a SUB_PROCESS node with a declared interface creates exactly one child instance whose initial variable map contains ONLY the declared inputs -- a parent variable not named in inputs is demonstrably absent from the child
a SUB_PROCESS node with no declared interface copies the full parent variable map to the child (EXT-05 behaviour preserved), demonstrated by an explicit test alongside the filtered case

each of the four SPC-01 failure modes has its own test and its own distinct error: the two activation failures leave ZERO child instances created (verified by counting instance rows), and the two completion failures leave the parent's variable map unmodified (no partial merge)

on child completion with a declared interface.outputs, only the named outputs merge into the parent via REQ-049's merge, and a child variable not named in outputs is demonstrably absent from the parent afterwards

the parent token's waiting_child_instance_id is set while the child runs and cleared on completion, and it survives a transition that copies tokens for an unrelated reason -- an explicit regression test for R-Co's GH #428 field-dropping bug
child instance creation is not reachable through REQ-045's public create/1 path, matching R-Co's internal-only createWithParentInheritance shape, confirmed by inspection and stated in the moduledoc
cancelling a parent instance does not cancel its running child, matching R-Co's documented EE-08 behaviour, demonstrated by an explicit test rather than assumed

each of the four SPC-01 failure modes is demonstrated routing into REQ-061's set_instance_error rather than writing its own ERROR transition, confirmed by inspection and by test -- this closes REQ-061's own AC obligation, deferred forward because REQ-062 did not exist when REQ-061 was built
all migrations apply cleanly against a fresh DB
no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user data
all callers of any changed function signature compile

result.summary:
REWORK ITERATION 3 (this pass): fixed both bugs this iteration was scoped to. (a) CaseClauseError in Letflow.Engine.append_sub_process_completion_cascade_multi/6 (engine.ex:1678) and the identical pattern in Letflow.Engine.SubProcess.maybe_cascade_to_grandparent/7 (sub_process.ex:922): both `case Map.fetch!(changes, lookup_key) do` statements matched on `{:ok, nil}` / `{:ok, %TokenRecord{} = parent_token}`, but Ecto.Multi.run/3 stores the UNWRAPPED ok-value in `changes`, not the {:ok, _} tuple the callback itself returns (find_waiting_parent_token/3 returns {:ok, token}, Multi stores just `token`) -- so the real runtime value hitting the case statement was a bare %TokenRecord{} (or bare nil), matching neither clause. Root cause was NOT a Token-vs-TokenRecord struct-shape mismatch as hypothesized in the rework instruction -- it was this {:ok, _} double-wrapping bug, confirmed by the actual crash payload (`no case clause matching: %Letflow.Engine.TokenRecord{...}`, not wrapped in a tuple). Fixed both sites by matching the raw value (`nil` / `%TokenRecord{} = parent_token`) instead of the tuple form, with a comment at each site explaining why. (b) Added `@derive Jason.Encoder` to Letflow.EventStore.Registry.ValidationFailure (lib/letflow/event_store/registry/validation_failure.ex) -- no comparable struct in this codebase already derives Jason.Encoder (checked; Letflow.Engine.ExecutionError itself builds a plain map and calls Jason.encode!/1 directly rather than deriving), so used the derive form directly per Jason's own recommended convention; all three fields (field_path, constraint, actual) are already non-sensitive, already-decoded terms per the struct's own moduledoc, so deriving the full struct is safe.

Verification: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> 'Compiling 3 files (.ex), Generated letflow app' (exit 0). `mix format --check-formatted` on all three touched files -> clean, no output. `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs test/letflow/engine_test.exs` -> '42 tests, 6 failures' (same count as before this pass, but a DIFFERENT set of underlying causes -- see below). Confirmed both assigned bugs are actually gone: zero occurrences of CaseClauseError or Protocol.UndefinedError/Jason.Encoder anywhere in the scoped run's output. `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine_test.exs` alone -> '32 tests, 0 failures' (fully green, no regression).

NOT fully green: fixing the two assigned bugs let execution proceed further into EngineSubProcessTest's completion-cascade path and exposed THREE further, distinct problems -- none of them the two bugs this iteration was scoped to fix, and none of them touched by this pass's changes:
(i) Ecto.Multi key collision: `** (RuntimeError) cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [:task_records]` -- both Letflow.Engine's own top-level Multi (for the completing child task, via build_task_activation_and_reconciliation_multi) and Letflow.Engine.SubProcess.build_completion_write_steps/12 (invoked when the cascade reaches the parent) call TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6 which always appends under the SAME fixed atom key `:task_records` (lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex:246) regardless of which instance it's for -- when the cascade folds the parent's own Multi.merge/2 result into a Multi that already has a `:task_records` step from the child's own completion, Ecto's own static merge-key-collision check fires. Fixing this needs a real signature change (namespacing the Multi key by instance_id at every one of append_multi_from_existing_records's call sites, including the grandparent-cascade recursion in sub_process.ex), which is a structural change beyond 'fix these two case statements' -- did not attempt it, per the rework instruction's explicit 'no strategy change is required, just fix both [the two named bugs]'. Affects AC4 and AC5's own child-completion tests (2 of the 6).
(ii) `** (DBConnection.ConnectionError) transaction rolling back` on the two output-side interface-violation tests (SUB_PROCESS_MISSING_REQUIRED_OUTPUT, SUB_PROCESS_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION) -- consistent with the same idempotency_key-collision disease iteration 2 already fixed for INSTANCE_STARTED/SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED, but NOT yet applied to the EXECUTION_ERROR event path: when append_completion_multi's build_parent_merge_variables/2 rejects the child's output, it calls ExecutionError.append_multi(error_args, ...) with `idempotency_key` still the caller's raw, unmodified complete_task/3 request key (see to_error_args call sites in sub_process.ex, both pass `idempotency_key` through verbatim) -- the SAME key already claimed earlier in the SAME transaction by the child's own TASK_COMPLETED event, so EventStore.append/2's nested transaction hits its own claim_idempotency collision and Postgres aborts the outer transaction, surfacing as a generic 'transaction rolling back' on whatever query runs next. Not confirmed by direct instrumentation this pass (out of assigned scope, not touched) but the mechanism matches iteration 2's own documented root-cause pattern closely enough to name with confidence rather than leave unexplained. Affects AC3/AC8's two output-side failure-mode tests (2 of the 6).
(iii) Pre-existing, already flagged by iteration 2's own report as 'a related but distinct reason' and explicitly left untouched: the two INPUT-side interface-violation tests (SUB_PROCESS_MISSING_REQUIRED_INPUT, SUB_PROCESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION) assert `{:ok, result} = Engine.complete_task(gate_task.id, ...)` (the gate task's own completion should succeed, with the resulting :error routing happening internally via set_instance_error per AC8), but the call actually returns `{:error, {:instance_execution_error, :subprocess_interface_violation, {:field, "amount"}}}` -- an unhandled error propagating out of complete_task/3 instead of being absorbed into a successful call whose SIDE EFFECT is the instance flipping to :error. This is unrelated to (i)/(ii) above (confirmed: it was already failing this exact way in the very first scoped run this pass took, before either of this pass's two fixes were applied) and is not a new regression from this pass's changes. Affects the 2 remaining tests.

Did not touch test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs per the rework instruction. rework_count is now 3/3 (max_rework) -- per the rework instruction, reporting PARTIAL rather than PASS since the scoped run is not fully green; escalation past ELIXIR-DEV is expected next, per the instruction's own framing ('escalation follows if this doesn't land').
issues: OQ-3 (design's own, not newly introduced): nested/grandchild SUB_PROCESS activation is not recursively wired -- unchanged from prior passes, still flagged in Letflow.Engine.SubProcess's moduledoc.

A PARALLEL_GATEWAY split/join branch landing directly on a SUB_PROCESS node is still explicitly rejected with {:sub_process_after_split_join_not_supported, token_id} -- unchanged from prior passes, mirrors the codebase's own pre-existing {:new_token_during_resume_not_supported, _} limitation.

NOT fixed this pass (out of this iteration's assigned scope -- a real signature change, not a case-clause fix): Ecto.Multi key collision -- TaskActivation.append_multi_from_existing_records/6 (lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex:246) always appends under the fixed atom key :task_records regardless of instance; when the sub-process completion cascade folds the parent's own Multi (built by SubProcess.build_completion_write_steps/12) into a Multi that already has a :task_records step from the child's own completion, Ecto.Multi.merge/2 raises 'cannot merge Multi; the following operations were found in both Ecto.Multi: [:task_records]'. Needs the Multi key namespaced by instance_id at every append_multi_from_existing_records call site (including the grandparent-cascade recursion in sub_process.ex). Blocks AC4 and AC5's own child-completion tests (2 of the remaining 6).

NOT fixed this pass (out of scope): 'transaction rolling back' (DBConnection.ConnectionError) on the two output-side interface-violation tests -- consistent with the same idempotency_key-collision pattern iteration 2 already fixed for INSTANCE_STARTED/SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED, but not yet applied to the ExecutionError event path: when SubProcess.append_completion_multi's build_parent_merge_variables/2 rejects the child's output, to_error_args passes the caller's raw, unmodified idempotency_key through to ExecutionError.append_multi -- the same key already claimed earlier in the same transaction by the child's own TASK_COMPLETED event -- so EventStore.append/2's nested transaction hits its own claim_idempotency collision. Not confirmed by direct instrumentation this pass; named by pattern-match to iteration 2's own documented root cause, not verified line-by-line. Blocks AC3/AC8's two output-side failure-mode tests (2 of the remaining 6).

Pre-existing, NOT newly introduced by this pass (already failing this exact way before either of this pass's two fixes were applied, per this pass's own first scoped run): the two input-side interface-violation tests (SUB_PROCESS_MISSING_REQUIRED_INPUT, SUB_PROCESS_INPUT_SCHEMA_VIOLATION) assert the gate task's own complete_task/3 call succeeds ({:ok, result}, with the :error routing happening internally per AC8's set_instance_error contract), but it actually returns {:error, {:instance_execution_error, :subprocess_interface_violation, {:field, "amount"}}} -- an unhandled error propagating out instead of being absorbed into a successful call. Blocks the remaining 2 of 6.
result.next_action: rework_count is now 3/3 (max_rework) -- no further ELIXIR-DEV rework iteration is available on this handoff per the sizing rule; ORCH/next-agent escalation required. The scoped run (test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs + test/letflow/engine_test.exs) is 36/42 passing (engine_test.exs itself is fully green at 32/32; all 6 remaining failures are in EngineSubProcessTest). This iteration's two assigned bugs (CaseClauseError in the sub-process completion cascade, missing Jason.Encoder on ValidationFailure) are confirmed fixed and no longer appear anywhere in the scoped run's output. Three further distinct, unfixed problems remain, none introduced by this pass and none part of its assigned scope -- see result.issues for full detail: (i) an Ecto.Multi :task_records key-collision needing a real signature change across task_activation.ex and sub_process.ex, (ii) a suspected idempotency_key collision on the ExecutionError event path (same disease iteration 2 fixed elsewhere, not yet applied here), and (iii) a pre-existing bug where input-side interface violations return {:error, ...} instead of {:ok, ...} from complete_task/3. Recommend the next step be a fresh CODE-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV cycle scoped explicitly to these three (particularly (i), which needs a design decision on how Multi keys should be namespaced across the cascade), rather than a fourth same-shape rework iteration on this handoff.
